key_insight: The paper combines dispersive hyperbolic water-wave models offshore with the shallow water equations near shore to capture tsunami physics efficiently and robustly.
engineering_relevance: This enables scalable tsunami simulation with better accuracy than non-dispersive shallow-water models while keeping computational cost low enough for large, adaptive GeoClaw runs.
method: Use two hyperbolic reformulations of the Serre-Green-Naghdi equations in deep water.
Switch to the non-dispersive shallow water equations near the shoreline.
Implement the coupled model in GeoClaw with adaptive mesh refinement and shared-memory parallelism.
evidence_signal: The approach is validated against benchmarks and real tsunami data, and it achieves about a 2x speedup over GeoClaw’s existing dispersive solver in a large-scale tsunami simulation.
watch_item: Accuracy and stability depend on the coupling between dispersive and shallow-water regions, so the transition strategy and implementation details need careful tuning.
paper_title: Adaptive, efficient, and scalable water wave modeling with dispersive hyperbolic systems
